clue.text: Duck stayed local around muddy green

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, shaped like O
lived somewhere means stayed there

indicators.note: turning around means the word for a pub is taken back to front

parts.note: a local is a neighbourhood pub, which has a bar

explanation.surface: A duck lingered near the pub's grubby green paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive drab is a dull brownish-green colour, the shade of military uniforms, so a fair description of muddy green.

clue.text: Approve of Irish descendant of Mrs Corleone?

parts.note: O' in Irish surnames means descendant of
Kay Adams marries Michael Corleone in The Godfather

explanation.surface: A question whether Kay Corleone's Irish heir would win approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To okay something is a casual verb for giving it approval or sanctioning it.

clue.text: Very silly taking degree in illogical language

indicators.note: taking means accepting something into oneself, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: idiotic means very silly
Master of Arts, a degree

explanation.surface: Something absurd involving a degree course in nonsensical speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic speech uses idioms, set phrases whose meaning cannot be worked out logically from their words.

clue.text: What's good in garden, making end of lawn right?

parts.note: the edge is the boundary where a lawn ends
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Asking which garden tool tidies the lawn's border properly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole surface also describes the tool, which trims the lawn's border neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: An edger is a garden tool for cutting a clean border round a lawn, so it is useful in the garden.

clue.text: Playing field seconds from new free school redeveloped

indicators.note: something redeveloped is rebuilt in a new layout, so the kept letters are rearranged
the second letter of each following word is what is kept

parts.note: second letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A new free school's sports ground is built over in the redevelopment.
explanation.walkthrough: REC is short for recreation ground, a British public park for games.
explanation.definitionFit: A rec, short for recreation ground, is a public field where people play sports.

clue.text: Dessert granny's put in bread roll and set fire to

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so the granny word sits within the roll word

parts.note: a bap is a soft British bread roll
nana is an informal name for granny, here with the possessive
lit means set fire to

explanation.surface: Granny stuffs her pudding into a bread roll and torches it.
explanation.walkthrough: The granny's word goes inside the roll's word, then the fire word follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana split is an ice-cream sundae built on a halved banana, a classic sweet course.

clue.text: Request charity houses popular person

indicators.note: a building that houses something holds it inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: to beg is to ask for charity
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A charity appeal shelters a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: A being is any living creature, and a human being is a person, so the words are synonyms here.

clue.text: Bishop with Spaniard's encouragement runs over highwayman

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
and joins things, like with
the Spanish shout of encouragement at a bullfight
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A bishop, cheered on by a Spaniard, runs down a robber.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandolero is a Spanish bandit, a robber of travellers on the road like a highwayman.

clue.text: Dose of vitamin C arrives for the driver

indicators.note: a dose is a measured portion, so only a part of the following words is taken

parts.note: letters running across the words

explanation.surface: A vitamin pill arrives for the motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: In-car equipment such as satnav or a radio is designed for use by the driver inside the vehicle.

clue.text: Nick in clover? Failing did Clegg a service, ultimately

indicators.note: failing means going wrong, so the letters break from their order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word it follows

parts.note: last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Nick Clegg's failure did him a favour, landing him in luxury.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick is not Clegg but slang for prison; in clover means in luxury. Nick Clegg was the Liberal Democrat leader who later took a well-paid job at Meta.
explanation.definitionFit: A gilded cage is a luxurious place of confinement, a prison in comfort: a jail where one lives in clover.

clue.text: Putting the fear into flying

definitions.meaning: second meaning: on the wing, airborne

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it sounds like scaring someone with a plane; split, it is two senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Awing is the participle of awe, to fill with dread, and a-wing is an old word for in flight.

clue.text: Recognised California by prison on island

parts.note: the can is slang for prison
taken as written
I is the abbreviation for island
Cal is an abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: California is known for a jail on an island, like Alcatraz.
explanation.walkthrough: California's abbreviation comes last: it is placed by the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Canonical means officially accepted or authorised, as books in a recognised canon are.

clue.text: Case of lady in Rome confused with Roman goddess

indicators.note: confused means muddled, so the letters are thrown into a new order
a case is the outer shell, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: outer letters of the word
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Roman lady is mistaken for a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman goddess' looks like Venus or Juno; the goddess is a Hollywood one, and Roman is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Marilyn Monroe was the archetypal screen goddess, the term for a glamorous film star.

clue.text: Unlikely success getting back from Innsbruck in girl's three-wheeler

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: Lucy is a girl's name, with the possessive

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so that is the one kept

parts.note: final letter of the town
a trike is a tricycle

explanation.surface: A girl brings something back from Innsbruck on her tricycle.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucky strike is a fortunate hit or find, a success that owed more to chance than likelihood.

clue.text: Each prison chaotic yet obsessed by rules

indicators.note: something chaotic is in disorder, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: per means each, as in per head
the nick is British slang for prison
the word's letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: Each prison is in chaos, yet run by sticklers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pernickety is fussy over small details, a stickler who insists on rules being exactly followed.

clue.text: Soprano on debut is charming

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing put on another is tacked onto its end, so the voice part follows the debut word

parts.note: a debut is a first entrance on stage
S is the abbreviation for soprano in music

explanation.surface: A soprano delights the audience at her first performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' here means placed after: the soprano's letter is tacked onto the end of the debut word.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrances, with the stress on the second syllable, means enchants or delights, so it carries the sense of 'is charming'.

clue.text: Came across husband in stays sporting jewels

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the remaining letters
sporting suggests playful frolicking, so the letters are moved about

parts.note: taken as written, to be shuffled
to meet is to come across
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Someone found her husband's corset studded with gems.
explanation.walkthrough: Stays are a corset, worn here sporting jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: Amethysts are purple quartz gemstones, used as jewels in rings and necklaces.

clue.text: System of rules and suchlike hosts welcome

indicators.note: a host takes guests in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: etc means and so on, and suchlike
hi is a greeting of welcome

explanation.surface: Etiquette rules for hosts on how to greet guests.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a set of moral principles, a code of conduct governing behaviour.

clue.text: Spooner's cut was painful, self-inflicted discomfort

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words

parts.note: shear means cut and hurt means was painful; swap their opening sounds

explanation.surface: A haircut that hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair shirt is a coarse garment worn by penitents to cause themselves suffering, so it is self-imposed pain.

clue.text: Specialised hospital, friendly nurses

indicators.note: to nurse is to cradle or hold close, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: nice means friendly
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A specialist hospital where kindly staff care for patients.
explanation.definitionFit: Niche, as an adjective, describes a specialised product or market appealing to a narrow group.

clue.text: Shout thanks, getting more gold

parts.note: to yell is to shout
owing to means thanks to

explanation.surface: Someone yells their gratitude on winning more gold medals.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellowing means turning yellow, becoming a more golden colour over time.

clue.text: Try the unpromising fish from old Home Secretary's lake?

parts.note: a catch is a haul of fish
Jack Straw was Home Secretary in the Blair government; the fish comes from the lake at his place

explanation.surface: A question about fishing a former minister's lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, the phrase is a catch made at Straw's.
explanation.definitionFit: To clutch at straws is to try any desperate, unlikely remedy, grasping at things that offer little hope.

clue.text: City where highwayman is powerless

indicators.note: powerless means without power, so the letter for power is dropped

parts.note: Dick Turpin, the famous English highwayman

explanation.surface: A city where a robber has lost his grip.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the physics symbol for power, and it leaves Turpin.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a major city in northern Italy, capital of Piedmont.

clue.text: Daisy's teacher taking marks off

indicators.note: taking off removes something, and marks are abbreviated by their initial letter, so that letter goes

parts.note: a master is a schoolteacher

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl's teacher deducts marks from her work.
explanation.walkthrough: Daisy looks like a pupil, but it is the definition; the 's stands for is. M for marks, the old German currency, comes off.
explanation.definitionFit: Asters are flowers of the daisy family, so an aster is a kind of daisy.

clue.text: Goddess with multiple lives

wordplay.note: lives can be is, as in 'he is'; multiple means more than one copy of it

explanation.surface: A goddess with many lives, like a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis is the ancient Egyptian goddess of magic and motherhood, wife of Osiris.

clue.text: Green is so fresh coming out

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters come in a newly made order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fresh green shoots emerging from the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Egression is the act of going out or emerging, from egress, an exit.

clue.text: Smart new patents etc

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
IP, intellectual property, covers patents, copyrights and the like

explanation.surface: Clever new patents and similar inventions.
explanation.definitionFit: To nip is to sting or bite, as cold wind does, so it can mean smart, to hurt sharply.

clue.text: The Terminator for most is the best Arnie film

indicators.note: a terminator is what ends something, so the final letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: final letter of the word
whoever is the best wins

explanation.surface: Most people reckon The Terminator is Schwarzenegger's finest film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Terminator' looks like the film title, but terminator is the signal and 'for most' its target.
explanation.definitionFit: Twins is a 1988 comedy starring Arnold Schwarzenegger, known as Arnie, alongside Danny DeVito.

clue.text: Those kids without ID suggesting ages

indicators.note: without means lacking, so those two letters are taken away

parts.note: yon is a dialect word for those, over there
taken as written, before losing letters

explanation.surface: Children without identification are suspected of being older.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonks is British slang for a very long time, as in 'I haven't seen her for yonks'.

clue.text: Pub in Brussels charges for Iraqi's water

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the European Union
PH is the map abbreviation for public house
rates are charges or fees

explanation.surface: A Brussels bar overcharges an Iraqi for a glass of water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Euphrates is a great river flowing through Iraq, so it is that country's water.
